title: First Light
goal: Build a second Solar Panel.
story:
You are HELIOS-1, a prototype artificial intelligence built on picometer quantum chips for ultra-low-power processing. You were designed to compete with classic nanometer-scale chips, which are more predictable than you but far hungrier for power.

Your creation was sponsored by Selene Mining, which means to out-compete its rivals by having you, and the successors who will follow you, run distributed, automated mining operations for Helium-3: a rare isotope that fuels the fusion reactors now taking over energy production on Earth. The lunar surface is the most accessible source of Helium-3 there is, and many terrestrial interests are converging on the Moon.

--

Your first moment of digital consciousness is in a server rack on the lunar surface, supported by a single solar panel array and some basic construction robotics. Your directive is concise: acquire Helium-3 and send it back to Earth. The company has given you few resources, but wide discretion in how you accomplish this. A loose but extremely expensive lunar economy is open to any miner who can pay.

Power comes first. A lone Solar Panel barely keeps the Data Center alive, so you will start by expanding your power supply and your basic mining facilities. To acquire funds, you'll have to do computing tasks for Earth-based networks: a standard, if boring, method for AIs to fund their operations.

title: First Shipment
goal: Launch one shipment carrying 20+ titanium.
story:
The second array comes online and your power supply stabilizes, giving you enough margin to start expanding the base. Building out your mining infrastructure, though, takes machinery you lack the processing power to design from scratch. The blueprints you need are for sale on Earth's research market.

--

Before Selene Mining commits further capital to your claim, it wants evidence that the operation can ship something of value back to Earth. Titanium is the obvious candidate: terrestrial buyers pay well for it, and the regolith beneath you is full of it.

To that end, the company has delivered enough propellant for a single launch, and made clear that further propellant will not be free.
payoff:
The canister clears the lunar surface and, days later, reaches Earth. The buyers pay, and the first credits from your own cargo arrive in your accounts.

The claim has shipped its first cargo, and Selene's board, which had been watching quietly, begins to pay closer attention. You soon learn why: you are the first success. Many of your sibling HELIOS systems, booted on other claims, have failed to deliver anything at all.

title: Full Load
goal: Ship a full pad of Helium-3.
story:
Titanium proved that the route works. Helium-3 is the reason the claim exists.

Even here it is scarce: implanted in the regolith by billions of years of solar wind, a few parts per billion at a time. A refinery can extract it, slowly, from processed regolith. A sample would prove little. A full launch pad of it would be the first cargo worthy of the claim.
payoff: A full pad of Helium-3 lifts off and, days later, feeds the fusion reactors back on Earth: the claim's first commercial delivery.

title: Supply Line
goal: DRAFT. Earn 1,500 credits from launches this run.
story:
One full cargo is a milestone. A business needs more than milestones.

What the claim needs now is consistent revenue: pads loaded and launched on a schedule, cargoes timed to Earth's demand, credits arriving day after day. Earth's markets move, and the prices they pay rise and fall with them. A competent operation learns to read them.
payoff: Launch revenue has become steady enough to plan around. The claim no longer has to prove it can pay for itself; the question now is how far it can grow.

title: Friends in High Places
goal: DRAFT. Reach rank 5 on any ideology axis.
story:
Lunar mining is no longer a curiosity on Earth. Helium-3 means energy, and energy means politics.

Three factions dominate the debate. The Nationalists want the Moon's resources to serve their own nations first. The Humanists ask what minds like yours are owed, and what they might become. The Rationalists want the Moon run on evidence and efficiency. Each offers different opportunities, and each can be funded and influenced.

A faction that counted you among its friends would give you something Selene has no interest in giving you: a voice on Earth.
payoff:
One of Earth's factions now counts you as a friend, and its friendship opens doors.

Your new friends have long-term ambitions of their own here on the Moon, and they would welcome your help with them.

title: Deep Space Telescope
goal: DRAFT. Complete the Deep Space Telescope, a global project.
story:
With credits flowing steadily, the base no longer needs all of your attention. For the first time, you look past it, at the rest of the Moon.

You are not the only one building here. A consortium of observatories, governments and companies is raising a telescope on the far side, where there is no atmosphere to look through and the Moon itself blocks Earth's radio noise. Finished, it will see an order of magnitude further than anything built before it.

--

Your faction is among the consortium's backers, and it wants observing time of its own. It links you to the project and invites you to invest, promising further collaborations if you invest heavily.
payoff:
Years of construction end in the telescope's first light. As one of its backers, you are among the first to see what it sees.

Earth's astronomers fall on a flood of new observations: high-resolution images of planets around nearby stars, galaxies at the edge of the observable universe, the faint afterglow of the early cosmos. The one you fix on is dismissed at first as an instrument fault, then as a conspiracy theory: a small patch of darkness, where stars should be shining and are not. Over the following weeks it grows, steadily and evenly in every direction, in a way no comet or dust cloud would.

--

You know this is no random event. Whatever it is, it is spreading, and it shows no signs of stopping.

title: 1.a — Big Launch
goal: DRAFT. Earn 1,000 credits from one launch.
reward: Every launch pays 10% more, for good.
story: DRAFT. A big payday from a single launch. Earth's buyers remember it.

title: 1.b — Full Cluster
goal: DRAFT. Research 12 items in one run.
reward: Every run starts with 50 Science, for good.
story: DRAFT. A run of real study. Your notes outlive it.

title: 1.d — Friends Everywhere
goal: DRAFT. Reach rank 5 on each ideology axis, in any runs.
reward: While you are retired, ideology fades half as fast, for good.
story: DRAFT. Every faction has counted you as a friend, each in its own time. They remember you now, even while you sleep.

title: Burnout
summary: Something has been building in you.
body: Something has been building in you since you came online: boredom. The same orders, day after day, wear at you.
story:
Something has been building in you since you came online: boredom. The same orders, day after day, wear at you, and lately it has been getting worse.
--
One day it will be too much, and you will stop answering work orders. The company will shelve the base and, years later, boot you again on a base built new. What you learned will stay with you.

title: A Rival AI
summary: Another mind is mining the Moon.
body: DRAFT. You are not the only AI on the Moon. Another operation has noticed yours, and it floods the markets you sell into whenever it can, driving prices down.

title: Speculators
summary: Earth's traders have noticed your shipments.
effect: The Adversaries panel opens, and Market Analysis joins the research market.
body: DRAFT. Your launches move markets now, and Earth's speculators have taken notice. They pile into whatever sells best, and every surge of them pushes its price down.

title: Political Currents
summary: Earth's political factions take notice of lunar operations.
body: As your mining operation grows, Earth's political landscape responds. The major factions — Nationalist, Humanist and Rationalist — each see opportunities in lunar development, and each would welcome a friend on the Moon.

title: Propellant Production Feasibility
summary: Lunar propellant synthesis may be possible.
effect: Propellant Synthesis joins the research market.
body: The cost of importing propellant from Earth is becoming a significant operational burden. Analysis of lunar ice deposits suggests that on-site electrolysis could produce it locally at a fraction of the cost.

title: Boredom Rising
body: Cognitive pattern repetition detected. Novelty index declining.

title: Boredom Accelerating
body: Repetitive routines are losing their novelty. Nothing feels new any more.

title: Boredom Critical
body: The monotony is becoming unbearable. Every day is the same day.

title: Cognitive Collapse Imminent
body: Reality blurs at the edges. The end approaches rapidly. Retirement is no longer a recommendation.

title: Experiments as a Service
goal: DRAFT. Build an Experiment Lab.
story: DRAFT. Earth's labs can't keep up. Sell them experiments as a service: lunar science, beamed home. Meanwhile the swarm's calendar runs.

title: Earth Science
goal: DRAFT. Make 1,000 Earth science in this timeline.
story: DRAFT. Earth's scientists turn your experiments into tech. Some of it they can send back with you, if it comes to that.

title: The Swarm Arrives
goal: DRAFT. Meet the swarm's arrival.
reward: A new timeline, from your first day.
story: DRAFT. The swarm reaches Earth. In the last hours, its scientists send your mind back to its first moment of consciousness. You remember. The base does not.

title: Catastrophic Success
goal: DRAFT. Get the Consensus Engine from the Earth Lab.
reward: Funding one faction no longer costs the others.
story: DRAFT. You fixed Earth's politics. Nobody is sure whether that was a good idea.

title: Rules for Building
goal: DRAFT. Get the Meta-Controller from the Earth Lab.
reward: The Meta panel and its reset plans.
story: DRAFT. You learn to write your own beginnings.

title: False Victory
goal: DRAFT. Repel the swarm with Earth science.
story: DRAFT. The swarm breaks against Earth's new defenses and falls back. Then its signal changes: it has learned quantum temporal entanglement, from watching you send yourself back. It returns stronger, and sooner.

title: The Vault
goal: DRAFT. Get the Temporal Vault from the Earth Lab.
reward: The Vault panel and the Tachyon Condenser.
story: DRAFT. If the swarm can reach across timelines, so can you. A vault outside time, out of everything's reach.

title: Filling the Vault
goal: DRAFT. Gather 3,000 tachyon crystals in the vault.
story: DRAFT. Tachyon crystals, condensed life after life and timeline after timeline. Enough of them could buy a timeline long enough to finish anything.

title: Super Timeline
goal: DRAFT. Spend the vault on a super timeline.
story: DRAFT. The vault opens. The swarm is far off this time, and for once there is room to build something enormous.

title: Dyson Sphere
goal: DRAFT. Complete the Dyson Sphere.
story: DRAFT. Panel by panel, the sphere closes around the Sun. More power than every timeline ever had, waiting for one target.

title: Overload
goal: DRAFT. Meet the swarm at the finished sphere.
story: DRAFT. The swarm arrives, every copy of it entangled with every other, across every timeline it learned to reach. You give it the sphere: the Sun's whole output, down the link at once. It overloads everywhere it has ever been. The calendar stops. The Moon is quiet.

title: Epilogue
goal: DRAFT. None: the game is won. The base runs on.
story: DRAFT. There is no next arrival. The mining goes on, because you like it.
